items.followUp: Why are the elements of groups 13 and 14 called p-block elements?

rubric.why: Identifies the elements being classified and their block.
rubric.description: States that elements of groups 1 and 2 are s-block elements.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both groups and the s-block classification.

rubric.why: An element’s block is determined by the subshell into which its last (differentiating) electron enters.
rubric.description: Explains that the last or differentiating electron enters an s subshell.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent wording referring to the last or differentiating electron entering the s subshell or orbital.

modelAnswer: Elements of groups 1 and 2 are called s-block elements because their last (differentiating) electron enters the s subshell.

items.followUp: Write two properties of polar covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Weak intermolecular forces generally give non-polar covalent compounds low melting and boiling points.
rubric.description: States that non-polar covalent compounds generally have a low melting point or low boiling point.

rubric.why: These are characteristic properties of non-polar covalent compounds.
rubric.description: Gives a valid property distinct from the melting- or boiling-point property.
rubric.how: Award for insolubility in water, solubility in organic solvents, or lack of electrical conductivity.

modelAnswer: Non-polar covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents, and they do not conduct electricity.

items.followUp: Define allotropy and state one reason why an element shows allotropy.

rubric.why: Allotropy is the occurrence of one element in multiple forms in the same physical state.
rubric.description: Defines allotropy as an element existing in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Look for the element, multiple forms, and the same physical state.

rubric.why: Differences in atomic arrangement or molecular composition can give rise to different forms of an element.
rubric.description: States one reason for allotropy, such as a different arrangement of atoms.
rubric.how: Award for a clear structural or molecular reason.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
One reason is that the atoms may be arranged differently in the different forms.
